title: Lemma Card
description: Open schema for Lemma cards. A card is one of four discriminated variants on `kind`. The discriminator is structural, not subject-area: PrincipleCard covers physics, chemistry, biology, climate, mathematics, engineering — they all share the same shape because the verification operations are universal. The actual subject area lives in `domain`.

id.description: Stable, lowercase, hyphen-separated. Becomes part of the URL once the card is published. Never reuse an id.

version.description: Semver. MAJOR for breaking convention changes (e.g. sign flip), MINOR for added expectedLimits, PATCH for typos / refs.

domain.description: Subject area for grouping. Free-form. Conventional values: physics-condensed-matter, physics-classical-mechanics, chemistry-thermodynamics, chemistry-stoichiometry, biology-population-dynamics, climate-radiative, mathematics-analysis, engineering-fluid-dynamics.

validationEnvelopes.description: Numerical bounds the engine asserts at runtime. Keys are domain-conventional (plasmonOmegaP, gEarth_m_per_s2, gasConstant_J_per_molK). Values are [min, max] tuples in conventional units.

relative.description: Maximum fractional spread across methods, about the mean.

absolute.description: Maximum absolute spread, in the observable's own unit.

gating.description: Whether disagreement fails the verdict. Default true; set false for observables reported but known to be method-sensitive.

basis.description: Why this tolerance — the citation or reasoning behind the number.

crossMethodTolerances.description: Agreement tolerances for comparing the SAME observable across independent methods. Keys match the output keys engines emit (as validationEnvelopes does). Distinct from validationEnvelopes: those bound one run's value absolutely, these bound the SPREAD between runs. Exactly one of relative/absolute per observable.

convergence.description: Qualifies how a claimed convergence order is measured. Exists because the engine was otherwise deciding a verdict with a number of its own: the per-level spread threshold separates 'this refinement study is not a clean power law' (warn) from 'the method converges at the wrong rate' (fail), and a number that flips a verdict belongs in the card with its reasoning, the same argument that gives crossMethodTolerances a basis. Omitted, the engine falls back to a documented default and SAYS SO in the verdict, so the provenance is never silent.

orderKey.description: Which validationEnvelopes key holds the expected order. Defaults to observedConvergenceOrder.

maxPerLevelSpread.description: How far consecutive per-level orders may spread before the sequence stops supporting an order estimate at all. Exceeding it yields warn (refuse to judge), never fail.

basis.description: Why this number — the reasoning behind the threshold.

seriesConditions.description: Conditions every reported sample must satisfy. Distinct from validationEnvelopes, which bounds a magnitude: these bound a SIGN or relation, which can be universal where a magnitude is not. That is why cards deliberately carrying no envelope can still carry these — a density of states has no system-independent range but cannot be negative in any material, at any k-mesh, under any smearing.

expr.description: Optional plain-ASCII expression for the right-hand side (e.g. "(1/2)*m*v**2"). When given with `symbols`, the engine derives the RHS dimensions from the formula and checks them against lhsDims, instead of trusting the declared rhsDims.

symbols.description: Optional map of symbol name to its dimension vector, used to derive `expr`'s dimensions (e.g. { "m": {"M":1}, "v": {"L":1,"T":-1} }).

limit.description: Machine form of `regime`. Present only when the regime is a genuine limiting process; a substitution is a different operation and must not be expressed here.

to.description: Limit point: '0', 'oo', '-oo', or a numeric literal.

target.description: Machine form of `expectedReducesTo` — what the limit should equal. Either a corpus card (which must then declare `formula`) or an inline expression.

substitute.description: Machine form of a regime that SETS a variable rather than taking it to a limit — e.g. 'y = 0'. Distinct from `limit` on purpose: a substitution and a limit disagree wherever the function is discontinuous at the point, so conflating them silently produces wrong answers. Maps symbol -> value.

solveFor.description: Machine form of a regime that asks for a ROOT rather than a limit — e.g. terminal velocity, which is the v where the net force vanishes, not the limit of the force expression. Solves expr = 0 for the named symbol.

fixedPoint.description: Machine form of a regime that names a STATIONARY POINT of a coupled system — the state at which every equation vanishes simultaneously. Distinct from `solveFor`, which roots a single expression: a fixed point of a two-equation system cannot be found from one equation, which is why the system is declared here rather than assumed.

system.description: The coupled equations, each set to zero at the fixed point.

of.description: Which quantity this equation governs, e.g. 'x' for dx/dt.

parameters.description: Names the coupled system introduces beyond the hypothesis's own declared symbols — a two-equation system carries parameters the single declared equation does not. Declared rather than inferred so that no name is bound by guesswork: several common physics parameter names (gamma, beta, zeta, lambda, pi) collide with functions and constants in the algebra system, and an unbound collision computes a different expression than the card declared.

conditions.description: Inequalities selecting WHICH fixed point is claimed, e.g. 'y > 0'. A coupled system usually has several stationary points, and verifying stationarity alone would accept an extinction point for a claim about coexistence. A condition that is demonstrably violated refutes the claim; one the algebra system cannot decide without sign assumptions leaves the stationarity verdict standing and is reported as unverified.

law.description: Which quantity the claim is about. Free-form, matching how `domain` works — a closed enum here was physics-only and forced non-physics cards to mislabel themselves. Conventional values: energy, momentum, charge, particle-number, total-spin, parity, mass, probability, lyapunov-function.

evolution.description: Machine form of how a declared quantity evolves under the system. `rate` of '0' is genuine conservation; a non-zero rate is a dissipation claim, which is what the corpus's cards actually assert — mechanical energy under drag, and a Lyapunov function under logistic predation. Checked by differentiating `quantity` along `system` and comparing against `rate`.

quantity.description: The conserved or dissipated quantity, e.g. total mechanical energy.

system.description: Time derivatives of the state variables the quantity depends on.

rate.description: Claimed time derivative of `quantity`. '0' means conserved.

parameters.description: Names this block introduces beyond the card's declared symbols.

DimVec.description: Canonical dimension vector. Each axis is an integer exponent. Omitted axes default to 0. L=length, T=time, M=mass, E=energy, Q=charge, Theta=temperature, N=count.

MachineFormula.description: Machine-readable form of formulaTeX. Optional and additive: formulaTeX stays the human-facing statement, this is what a program evaluates. Same grammar as the dimensional check's expr/symbols so the corpus has one expression language, not two. Required before a limit claim can name this card as what it reduces to.

symbols.description: Every free symbol in expr, mapped to its dimensions.

relation.description: What this expression actually encodes, in plain English. Required because `expr` need NOT be a transcription of formulaTeX: a card may state the integrated form for a human and the differential form for a machine. Without this a consumer assumes they are the same relation and compares two expressions that were never meant to match.

SeriesCondition.description: A condition every reported sample of a quantity must satisfy. Structured rather than an expression on purpose: an expression language would need a computer-algebra system to evaluate, which would make the check Python-only like the symbolic adapter. Every such claim in the corpus fits this shape without algebra.

where.description: Restricts which samples the claim covers. Load-bearing, not a nicety: `Im chi_0(omega > 0) <= 0` says nothing about negative frequencies, where Im chi is legitimately positive, so testing outside the declared domain would manufacture a violation the card never asserted.

basis.description: Why this condition holds — the reasoning a reviewer would check.
